You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily | Fed Decision Tonight; Coinbase Slumps 10.10%; Brent Above $108 (September 16, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve Dynamics
Rate-hike expectations build ahead of the decision and dot plot
The Federal Reserve releases its rate decision and Summary of Economic Projections at 02:00 Beijing time on September 17, followed by a press conference at 02:30.
Bloomberg reported on September 15 that meeting-linked interest-rate swaps largely priced in a 25-basis-point increase. If delivered, it would lift the federal funds target range to 3.75%–4.00%. The decision remains pending at this edition’s cutoff.
Beyond the immediate decision, investors will assess the dot plot and the Fed’s view of how rising energy costs affect inflation and growth.
Market Impact : The response of risk assets will depend not only on whether the Fed hikes, but also on whether its guidance implies more tightening than expected. Hawkish guidance could pressure technology valuations and crypto risk appetite; a milder path could provide relief.
International Commodities
Saudi cargo cancellations extend the supply disruption into deliveries
Reuters reported on September 15, citing trade and shipping sources, that Saudi Arabia had cancelled some September-loading crude cargoes for European customers and suspended loading at Yanbu.
The damaged East-West pipeline is a key route bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. Poland’s Orlen is seeking replacement supplies.
The US energy secretary said the pipeline could return within days, but repair and loading timelines remain uncertain.
Market Impact : Disrupted deliveries support oil prices while increasing procurement and transport costs. This creates contrasting earnings implications for energy producers and fuel-intensive businesses such as airlines, transport operators and manufacturers.
Macroeconomic Policy
CLARITY setback puts crypto regulatory certainty back in focus
On September 15, the Senate rejected cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R.3633, the CLARITY Act , by 49 votes in favor and 50 against.
This was a procedural vote to advance consideration of the bill—not its permanent termination or the suspension of existing crypto rules.
The legislation seeks to clarify digital-asset classifications and SEC–CFTC responsibilities. The setback leaves the timing of a unified market-structure framework uncertain.
Market Impact : Legislative delays can affect expansion expectations for exchanges, stablecoins and related financial services. Regulatory uncertainty alongside pre-Fed interest-rate pressure increases near-term volatility risks for crypto assets and associated equities.
II. Market Review
Commodities & Forex Performance
Spot gold : Approximately $4,282.69 per ounce.
Spot silver : Approximately $63.53 per ounce.
WTI crude oil futures : Indicative price of approximately $104.82 per barrel, October 2026 contract.
Brent crude oil futures : Indicative price of approximately $108.16 per barrel, November 2026 contract.
US Dollar Index (DXY) : Approximately 99.71.
Driver Analysis : Saudi export disruptions and replacement-supply costs are central to oil trading, while gold faces competing influences from safe-haven demand and interest-rate expectations. With DXY approaching 100, US retail sales and the subsequent Fed decision are the next major catalysts for currencies and precious metals.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : Approximately 75,805.01 USDT , down 2.69% over 24 hours.
ETH : Approximately 2,400.93 USDT , down 4.48% over 24 hours.
24-hour turnover : Approximately 395 million USDT for Bitget BTC / USDT spot and 283 million USDT for ETH /USDT spot; these figures cover only those pairs on that platform.
Large Buyers & Price–Volume Watch : In its September 14 disclosure, Strive reported buying 469 BTC during September 8–11 at an average of approximately $77,954, including fees. Bitmine disclosed the same day that it had acquired 27,180 ETH over the preceding week. These are previously disclosed purchases, not new buying today. Both assets remain under pressure, and platform turnover is not equivalent to large-investor net inflows or proof of market-wide accumulation.
Driver Analysis : ETH underperformed BTC over the quoted 24-hour period. The CLARITY procedural setback and uncertainty ahead of the Fed decision constrain risk appetite. Corporate purchases provide identifiable evidence of demand but do not, by themselves, establish a price bottom.
US Equity Index Performance
Dow Jones : Closed at 52,092.57, down 0.63%.
S&P 500 : Closed at 7,585.68, down 0.45%.
Nasdaq Composite : Closed at 25,981.57, down 0.78%.
Tech Giants Dynamics
NVDA : $212.17, up 0.57%.
AAPL : $331.34, down 0.52%.
MSFT : $497.12, down 1.64%.
GOOGL : $344.98, down 1.26%.
AMZN : $248.42, down 2.02%.
META : $670.24, up 0.70%.
TSLA : $356.58, down 0.67%.
[...]
Performance Summary & Driver Analysis : Using Alphabet’s Class A shares, five of the seven giants declined. Amazon led losses, followed by Microsoft and Alphabet, while Meta and Nvidia advanced. The divergence suggests that pre-Fed valuation pressure remains important without producing a uniform technology selloff. Amazon’s Middle East cloud recovery, Google’s voice-model launch and Meta’s custom-chip plans provide company-specific context, but no single headline fully explains a day’s share-price move.
[...]
Representative stocks : Coinbase (COIN) fell 10.10%; Circle (CRCL) declined 11.41%.
[...]
1. Coinbase (COIN) - A 10.10% slump resets regulatory expectations
[...]
Event Overview : Coinbase closed at $172.11 on September 15, down 10.10%. The Senate’s procedural setback for CLARITY coincided with broad weakness in crypto-related equities.
[...]
2. Amazon (AMZN) - Middle East cloud damage tests business resilience
[...]
Event Overview : Amazon closed at $248.42 on September 15, down 2.02%. Reuters reported that AWS still could not restore access to damaged infrastructure in Bahrain and one UAE availability zone. Many customers had recovered through migration or backups; this is not a worldwide AWS outage.
[...]
Investment Implications : Monitor restoration, customer retention, potential impairment or compensation disclosures, and AWS margin guidance. Broader technology trading and interest-rate expectations also matter for the stock.
[...]
Google released Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking on September 15. Its official developer changelog lists both real-time voice models as generally available through the Live API, expanding voice-interaction and AI application capabilities.
[...]
Media reports indicate that Meta plans to deploy its MTIA 450 custom AI chip in the first half of 2027, focusing on inference workloads. Testing and deployment remain ahead; planned capacity should not be confused with cost savings already achieved.
